subject: Data lifecycle variance request — scoped deletion + sampled log proof (Elysium Therapeutics)
messages:
From: Maya Gordon <security@elysiumtx.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@elysiumtx.com
Date: 2028-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: scoped deletion + sampled log proof for tenant ELX-39

Hi Stephanie / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As discussed, Elysium needs a documented variance from the standard 90-day debug-log TTL for a scoped subset of tenant artifacts related to a sensitive trial (ELX-39). Our auditors have asked for: a) an official acceptance of a temporary 180-day retention for the named dataset, b) the export and redaction proof of any PII removed before disposal, and c) a sampled proof-of-delete package for the logs that shows timestamps, keystore changes, and the deletion manifest.

Can you confirm what evidence Redwood can provide (SIG/CAIQ supplement or equivalent) and an estimated delivery date? If you need a template or list from our side, I can attach the auditor checklist.

Thanks,
Maya Gordon
Head of InfoSec — Elysium Therapeutics
security@elysiumtx.com

Attachment: elysium-deletion-request-20280614.pdf (PDF)

Next steps I propose:
- Ben will outline the technical artifacts we can export and how we produce an auditable deletion manifest.
- Kimberly will confirm whether the CAIQ/SIG supplement needs any additional attestation language for an exception.
- We’ll target an internal delivery of a first-draft evidence pack within 5 business days (target: 2028-06-21).

Could you confirm the exact tenant identifier(s) (if different from ELX-39) and the list of log streams you want in the sample (app-debug, inference-trace, kv-cache-snapshots, etc.)? Also please share the auditor checklist if possible — that helps make sure we hit the expected artifacts.

Subject: Re: Request: scoped deletion + sampled log proof for tenant ELX-39

Stephanie / Kimberly / Maya — technical summary of what we can provide and how: 

What we can deliver (scoped):
- Deletion manifest (SHA256-signed manifest listing object ids, deletion timestamps, deletion job id).
- Sampled export (redacted) of up to 3 days of log material from the specified streams, with PII fields redacted per Elysium's spec.
- Keystore rotation record showing key versions and rotation timestamps correlated to deletion jobs.
- Forensic index extract: a compact index (no raw message bodies) that auditors can use to validate object deletion without exposing customer payloads.

How we produce proof-of-delete:
1) Run a scoped export job that snapshots object ids for the tenant and the selected streams.
2) Perform redaction pipeline (PII rules + manual sampling) and produce a README describing redaction rules.
3) Execute the canonical deletion job — job output contains the deletion manifest and retention policy ID.
4) Hash and sign manifest; store signature in our sigstore with an audit trail.

Deliverables and timelines (proposed):
- Draft evidence README + manifest template: 2028-06-18
- First sampled proof archive (3-day sample): 2028-06-21
- Final signed manifest and audit artifacts: 2028-06-23

Open items / questions for Elysium:
- Exact list of streams to sample (default suggested: app-debug, inference-trace, kv-cache-snapshots).
- Redaction acceptance criteria — do you require token-level masking or full-field suppression for any fields?
- Any auditor-specific signature requirements (e.g., timestamp authority or external notary)?

Attachments referenced: sample-proof-export-README.txt (text)

Ben Carter
Security Engineering Lead — Data Forensics
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Reyes <legal@elysiumtx.com>
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Maya Gordon <security@elysiumtx.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T12:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped deletion + sampled log proof for tenant ELX-39

Hi all,

Quick legal note: Elysium requires an explicit holding period attribution and a signed attestation acknowledging the temporary extended retention window (180d) for the named dataset. Can Redwood provide a short attestation document that we can include in the audit packet? The attestation should reference the retention policy ID and the timeframe.

Also, our auditors prefer SHA256-signed manifests with the signing key identified and a human-readable README explaining redaction choices. If Redwood can use a timestamp authority (RFC 3161 or equivalent), that would be ideal but not mandatory.

Thanks,
Tom Reyes
Senior Counsel — Elysium Therapeutics
Attachment: elysium-auditor-checklist.pdf (PDF, provided separately)

Hi Maya / Tom — following up with confirmation and next steps from Redwood.

Summary of agreement:
- Redwood accepts a temporary 180-day retention for the scoped dataset (tenant ELX-39) tied to retention exception ID RWI-2028-ELX39.
- Deliverables (with provisional dates):
  • Draft evidence README + manifest template — 2028-06-18
  • Sampled proof archive (3-day sample, redacted) — 2028-06-21
  • Signed deletion manifest + sigstore proof — 2028-06-23
  • Final attestation document referencing policy RWI-2028-ELX39 — 2028-06-23

Operational notes & constraints:
- The sampled archive will contain redacted logs only; raw customer payloads will not be included. 
- We will provide hash-signed manifests; Redwood will also include a timestamp authority proof where available. If Elysium requires an external notary, please advise and we can evaluate options.
- A short attestation template is attached; please review and confirm any language changes by 2028-06-20 so we can finalize signatures.

Attachments: redwood-scoped-erasure-evidence.zip (contains manifest template, redaction README draft, and sample index)

Action items for Elysium:
1) Confirm final stream list for sampling by 2028-06-17.
2) Confirm redaction acceptance criteria and whether an external timestamping authority is required.

Thanks — we’ll proceed once you confirm the above.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
